source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. Deep mine tunnels and wet echoing caverns turned impossibly cool: a dark, jazzy urban-noir funk groove in E minor, "the coolest sewer in the world" energy. A deep walking-then-slap bass line locks with tight, crisp drums; staccato brass stabs and a funky clavinet answer each other; a smoky tenor saxophone or muted trumpet plays a sly, memorable minor melody. Dripping water echoes and a hint of metallic percussion like distant pickaxes. Stylish, sneaky, groovy, never scary. Tempo 96 BPM, 4/4 time, key of E minor. Instrumentation: walking and slap electric bass, tight dry funk drums, clavinet, brass section stabs, muted trumpet, tenor saxophone, rhodes electric piano, small metallic percussion, dripping echo. Form: bass groove intro, sax/trumpet theme over the groove, brass and clavinet call-and-response, walking bass break, theme again. Duration: 90 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
